subject: Deployment options - Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private (data residency)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Cc: rishi.malhotra@redwood.com
Date: 2026-03-01T10:14:00-08:00
Subject: Deployment options - hosted/dedicated/private (post-call recap)

Thanks again for the call this morning — great to learn more about GreenHealth's deployment and residency constraints. Quick recap + proposed next steps so we're all aligned:

Summary of requirements you shared:
- Data must remain in the EU for PHI-adjacent telemetry and customer data stores
- Minimal cross-border egress (no routing to US for backups or processing)
- Preference for a managed offering but open to dedicated/private when necessary for compliance

Quick notes on fits: 
- Hosted API: quickest to get started; we have EU-hosted regions (eu-west-1) and can provision projects in-region. By default we route compute and storage within the selected region, but there are optional cross-region failover behaviors we should discuss.
- Redwood Dedicated: reserved GPU pools that can be pinned to an EU region — good middle ground for predictable throughput and stronger isolation.
- Redwood Private (VPC/on-prem): full customer-controlled network and on-prem options; recommended where strict residency or no external egress is required.

Proposed next steps:
1) Tech deep-dive with Rishi (solutions) to validate network/IP flows and confirm whether you need Dedicated or Private. (Can we target Thu 3/4 or Fri 3/5?)
2) I will share SOC2 + DPA and an initial deployment questionnaire for your security/compliance team.
3) If Dedicated looks likely, we’ll prepare an estimate for EU reserved capacity and expected lead time.

Attachments: SOC2_report_2025.pdf, DPA_template_v3.docx, greenhealth_ma_questionnaire.xlsx

Thanks — Marissa
Marissa Cole

Subject: Re: Deployment options - hosted/dedicated/private (post-call recap)

Thanks Marissa — helpful recap. A few clarifying questions from our security and infrastructure teams:

1) For Hosted API: can you guarantee that all production requests and persistent storage will remain in the EU, including backups and logs? Our legal team is asking specifically whether any metadata or logs could be sent to the US for processing.
2) Is cross-region routing or failover something you enable by default? If so, can it be disabled per-customer?
3) For Dedicated capacity: are customer workloads fully isolated from other tenants at the network level? Is Dedicated deployed within our AWS account or managed by Redwood?
4) For Private (VPC/on-prem): what are the options for air-gapped deployments vs customer VPC with direct peering? Any reference architecture you can share?

We need answers to the above to decide whether Hosted is viable or whether we must proceed to Dedicated/Private. Can you also share SOC2 and your standard DPA (we will review today)? Finally — please include any notes on EU/FR-specific regulations you think are relevant.

Would be great to lock a time next week for a 45m technical call with our infra/security (we're in CET). Thu 3/4 10:00 CET works for us if you and Rishi can make it.

Best,
Olga
Head of Compliance, GreenHealth Systems

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Olga Ivanova <olga.ivanova@greenhealthsys.eu>, Martin Dupont <m.dupont@medtech.fr>
Cc: rishi.malhotra@redwood.com

Subject: Re: Deployment options - hosted/dedicated/private (post-call recap)

Hi Olga — thanks, great questions. Answers below at a high level; we’ll go into detail on the technical call (Thu 3/4 10:00 CET).

1) Hosted API residency: we operate region-specific hosted projects (e.g., eu-west-1). For projects provisioned in an EU region, request processing and persistent storage (models, KV caches, logs) remain in-region. That said, we do offer configurable cross-region failover for high-availability; it is not enabled by default per account and can be disabled if you require strict in-region-only handling.

2) Cross-region routing: not on by default. Failover is an opt-in policy and can be scoped per-tenant. We will document the exact behavior (DNS, routing, periodic replication windows) in the technical deep-dive.

3) Dedicated capacity: Dedicated is deployed in Redwood-managed infrastructure but can be provisioned in the EU and logically isolated to your organization (dedicated GPU pools, network controls). It does not run in your AWS account today; for strictest controls we recommend Private (VPC) or the on-prem package.

4) Private / VPC / on-prem: options include (a) customer VPC with private peering and Customer-controlled keys (KMS) and (b) on-prem air-gapped install. We have reference infra diagrams and a checklist for onboarding.

Next steps from our side:
- I’ve attached SOC2_report_2025.pdf and DPA_template_v3.docx (see links below).
- Rishi will run through network flows and confirm what blocking rules we need to honor to keep traffic in-region.
- I'll add Redwood's EU-specific compliance notes into the call deck.

Confirming Thu 3/4 10:00 CET for the technical call — Rishi, Stephanie: can you join?

Links:
- Security questionnaire: https://forms.redwood.com/g/greenhealth-deployment
- HubSpot: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/contact/98765

Best,
Marissa
